findings.where: W4 section 5 ("What does not change") against W3 sections 7, 9, 11 and 13
findings.claim_in_addendum: The six phases, their order and what each waits on; every prediction's count and shape (P1.1 gains the "10 and 11" / "11 only" mark on each row); the arms of phase 4; the skill map's rows; sections 7 to 13 of W3.
findings.finding: Sections 7 to 13 of W3 name file 10 as the authority four times, in the very places that decide what a judge's verdict means. W4 section 1 replaces only one sentence of W3 section 2 ("That sentence is replaced by this one"), so the definitions in section 7, the failure condition in section 9, the exclusion in section 11 and the trap in section 13 are left pointing at the file W4 has just displaced. Section 7 is where phase 1's judges are told what counts as a row holding and what counts as a contradiction; under W4 as drafted a judge would mark a row "contradicts" on file 10's words while the model is written to file 11.
findings.evidence: W3 section 7: "**A row of the model's word list holds** when file 10's quoted sentence, at the Part named, says what the row says in the theory's terms, read no wider than written. ... It **contradicts** when file 10 says otherwise in a sentence the judge quotes." W3 section 7 again: "with the holder quoted (a sentence of file 10, a result in the record, or a prediction of section 5 that could fail)". W3 section 9: "A judge showing that the programme's use of file 10 rests on one of the theory's own attack points (Part 0, A to E) as if it were settled." W3 section 11: "Where the model finds file 10 cannot reach one of the owner's unknowns, that is recorded as an ask for the owner". W3 section 13: "**Writing the word list rows wider than file 10 writes them, or at the wrong Part.**" W4 section 1: "W3 section 2 said \"Semantics file 10, frozen, read only. File 20 is set aside (S4) and nothing here rests on it.\" That sentence is replaced by this one:"
findings.what_would_show_wrong: A sentence of W4 replacing "file 10" in W3 sections 7 to 13, or a reading on which W4 section 1's replacement reaches every occurrence in W3 rather than the one sentence it quotes. I grepped W3 for "file 10" and read every hit (lines 7, 19, 33, 66, 72, 74, 78, 90, 99, 101, 135, 165, 166, 201, 221, 243) and W4 in full; W4 quotes and replaces one sentence only, and names section 12's ask as "unchanged".
findings.forced_edit: W4 section 5 must stop saying sections 7 to 13 are unchanged, and section 1's replacement must be extended to W3 section 7's two bullets ("file 10's quoted sentence", "when file 10 says otherwise", "a sentence of file 10"), section 9's "(Part 0, A to E)", section 11's "file 10 cannot reach" and section 13's trap, each reworded to the two-file rule with the "10 and 11" / "11 only" mark.

findings.where: W4 section 3, first bullet, against W3 section 1 ("What is asked, over what range"), section 6's contract row and section 10's free choices
findings.claim_in_addendum: And Part XIV, "Declared inputs", names "the system boundary and continuity of an attribution (Part XII)" among the inputs the semantics records and does not supply
findings.finding: W4 takes one of the three items in file 11's new "Declared inputs" paragraph and leaves out the middle one, which is the one that bears on W3's own scope decisions. File 11 also adds a whole new paragraph to Part III on scope. Together they give a holder to three things W3 had resting on nothing but the plan's own say-so: the declared range of section 1, the "stated scope" half of section 6's contract row, and the free-choice thresholds of section 10 - and they raise the bar on the last, since the theory now says what makes a restriction appropriate is criticizable, not merely free. Semantics log S76 names this item where W4 does not.
findings.evidence: File 11, Part XIV: "Besides the two primitives, some claims take stated inputs that the semantics records and does not supply: the obligations \\(O\\) and \\(P\\) of a repair, with the occasions each covers (Part XI); the scope of a contract and what makes a restriction appropriate (Part III); the system boundary and continuity of an attribution (Part XII)." File 11, Part III, new section "Scope, and a question that can be wrong": "A contract is a declared subset of the physically admitted changes, and a stated scope is what makes it one. ... What makes a restriction appropriate to the question asked is a substantive, criticizable part of the claim; the semantics records the restriction and supplies no rule that certifies it." File 10, Part III, "A question can be wrong": no such paragraph (it runs "A question may fail to pick out its alleged target..." straight to "What is prohibited is changing \\(C\\) or \\(\\mathcal Q\\) during an assessment without recording that the claim has changed."). W3 section 10: "where a threshold has no reason in the record it is a free choice and is marked so". Semantics log S76: "a \"Declared inputs\" paragraph in Part XIV names the obligations and their occasions, the scope of a contract, and the system boundary and continuity".
findings.mark: held (W3's stated range and its marked free choices now rest on Part XIV's declared-inputs paragraph and Part III's scope paragraph rather than on the plan's own word); provenance: built
findings.what_would_show_wrong: W4 naming scope anywhere. I grepped W4 case-insensitively for "scope": the only hits are line 9 and line 40, on "word list", not on scope. I also checked file 10 Part III and Part V: Part V's non-vacuity carries "excluded by a stated scope, not silently", so the idea is not wholly new - but the appropriateness sentence and the declared-input status are.
findings.forced_edit: Add a bullet to W4 section 3: W3 section 1's declared range, section 6's contract row and section 10's free-choice thresholds now rest on Part XIV's "the scope of a contract and what makes a restriction appropriate (Part III)" and on Part III's new scope paragraph; and note that the thresholds are now criticizable parts of the claim, not simply free.

findings.where: W4 section 2 ("what it does to M2") and section 5, against HV file 33 - the skill the phase 1 judges carry

findings.finding: It is gone from the theory and from the model, and it is still in the skill. HV file 33's word list maps the plain word *fitted* to file 10's Derivation 3 in its unqualified form, and `the-idea-in-depth.md` states it in plain words; the word list also declares file 10 its frozen source by name. Every part of W3 that carries provenance *fitted* (M2's consequence, M4, M6, M10) and every judge's mark in P1.4 runs through those two sentences. findings.where: W4 section 3, third bullet (M9 and the premise of the skill map), against W3 section 4's declared boundary and M9
findings.claim_in_addendum: So M9's claim that where an attention policy sits is decided by where the boundary is drawn is now on the theory's own words
findings.finding: File 11's new sentences make M9's wording false on W3's own declaration rather than holding it. W3 declares the transport program inside the system boundary; M9 then says a policy fixed in that same program is outside the declared boundary. Under file 10 nothing in the theory forced the issue. Under file 11, "a process run inside the boundary is the system's whoever wrote it" and "where the boundary is drawn decides, not where the process sits in the casing" make the two W3 sentences incompatible. W3 section 4 states the same point correctly ("outside what the reader can make a target"), so the fault is M9's phrase alone.
findings.evidence: W3 section 4: "*Boundary* \\(\\beta\\): the system is the reader and the program that hands it its context (the transport); the record, the corpus and the owner are outside it. Under this boundary a policy fixed in the transport's program is outside what the reader can make a target; a policy carried as text in the context is inside." W3 M9: "a policy fixed in the transport's program is outside the declared boundary and scrutinizable only by its designer." File 11, Part XII, "System boundary and continuity": "a process run inside the boundary is the system's whoever wrote it; a process run outside it is not the system's however close it sits." File 11, Part X, "Ownership": "where the boundary is drawn decides, not where the process sits in the casing."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: A second boundary declared in W3 under which the transport program is outside, or a reading of "the transport" in section 4 that excludes its program. W3 declares one \\(\\beta\\), and names "the program that hands it its context (the transport)" as the system; M9's "the transport's program" is the same object. I read both sentences in full and found no second declaration.
findings.forced_edit: W4 must record that M9's phrase "outside the declared boundary" is struck and replaced by section 4's own wording, "outside what the reader can make a target" - or, if M9 is meant as written, that \\(\\beta\\) is redeclared to put the transport program outside, which would change what arm (r) and P4.6 are measuring.

findings.where: W4 section 3, third bullet, against W3 section 6's premise ("A skill is a carrier of one or more of the theory's operations for an agent")
findings.claim_in_addendum: A skill's router table is "an instruction about what to read". ... a skill carried as text inside the boundary is the system's own today whoever wrote it, and the same skill supplied from outside is an outside contribution.
findings.finding: W4 quotes the whole Part X passage and then glosses only the clause that helps. The passage has two clauses pulling against each other, and W4 picks the one the skill-map premise needs. On W3's declared boundary the record and the owner are outside, so file 33 is "an instruction about what to read" supplied from outside, which the same passage says "remains an outside contribution however it is executed inside". The premise of section 6 is not held by this passage; it is held by a reading of it that the passage's other half denies.
findings.evidence: File 11, Part X, "Ownership": "Work supplied from outside that boundary, a diagnosis, a decisive question, an instruction about what to read, remains an outside contribution however it is executed inside; a process that runs inside the boundary is the system's own today whoever wrote it; and where the boundary is drawn decides, not where the process sits in the casing." W3 section 4: "the record, the corpus and the owner are outside it". W3 section 6: "\"A skill is a carrier of one or more of the theory's operations for an agent\" is not in file 10". W4: "Mark of M9 unchanged (held if, by P4.6); the premise of section 6 stays a construction, now with this passage among those that permit it."
findings.mark: held if (held only by one clause of a passage whose neighbouring clause cuts the other way; what would settle it is which side of \\(\\beta\\) file 33 is declared to sit on); provenance: built
findings.what_would_show_wrong: A W3 sentence putting file 33 inside \\(\\beta\\), which would make the "process that runs inside" clause the governing one. W3 section 4 names only the reader and the transport program as inside, and lists the record and the corpus as outside; file 33 is neither named. That is the gap.
findings.forced_edit: W4 must quote both clauses in its gloss and say that W3 nowhere declares which side of \\(\\beta\\) the skill file sits on, leaving section 6's premise a construction as before - not one the passage now permits.

verdict:
## 1. The question, frozen

What is explained: W4's claim that re-basing W3 on file 11 changes exactly what W4 names - one claim (Derivation 3, and M2 with it), the holders in its section 3, the five rewordings in its section 4 - and that everything else, including W3 sections 7 to 13, stands. Range: every sentence of file 11 that differs from file 10 and bears on a part M1 to M10, a row of W3 section 6, a prediction of section 5 or a definition of section 7; and, the other way, every sentence of file 10 that W3 relied on and file 11 drops or narrows. What is asked: rule-status (does the owner's header claim, read for this plan, mean what W4 takes it to mean) and purpose-achievement (does W4's device do the job it is for). Held still: files 10 and 11 as they stand, W3 as frozen, W4's draft as written, the record as logged.

One distinction the whole judgement turns on, and W4 does not draw it. File 11's header, Semantics S75 and S76 speak about **what the theory claims**. W4's section 3 is built on **what holds a sentence of W3**. The second can move while the first stands still: a sentence that was true-but-unstated in file 10 and is stated in file 11 changes no claim and changes a great many holders. Every finding below is of the second kind. **None of them contradicts file 11's header, and the owner's claim holds as written.** It does not do the work W4 asks of it: "nothing else is claimed differently" does not give "nothing else in W3 moves", and W4's section 3 is itself the proof that it does not.

## 2. The explanation in parts, and the jobs

W4's parts, in its words: (P1) "the theory this programme is written to is file 11, read beside file 10 ... and every quotation in phase 1's word list carries a mark, \"10 and 11\" or \"11 only\""; (P2) M2 restated under the qualified Derivation 3; (P3) section 3's list of sentences that now hold parts W3 marked construction or held-if; (P4) section 4's "Five, none changing a claim"; (P5) section 5's "What does not change", including "sections 7 to 13 of W3"; (P6) section 6's give-up list; (P7) the traps.

The jobs. **Given** (W4's own): find what rests on file 11 alone so it can be re-derived if round S76 fails; keep W3's phases, arms and predictions running unchanged. **Fixed** (by W3 section 11, Semantics S6, HV H8 and the root conventions): nothing in Semantics or in HV Skill is edited from here; a fault in the skill becomes an ask. **Added** (mine, and marked as mine): every sentence of W3 whose *holder* moved is named, not only those whose *claim* moved; every W3 quotation is still present in the new authority at the Part named. Both added jobs are the ones P3 and P4 exist to do, so testing against them is fair; a part held only by them is held relative to them, and I say so where it happens.

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Provenance | By what |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1, the two-file device with marks | held | built | It does the job the rival cannot: if S76 fails, the "11 only" rows locate what to re-derive. Its pattern is the Semantics project's own (S64's EARLIER / REVISED ONLY), and the owner's word W2 puts file 11 first. |
| P2, M2 restated | held | built | The qualification is quoted correctly from file 11's Derivation 3, Part IV and Part XII; the independence premise survives word for word; attack point (D)'s new form is quoted exactly. |
| P3, the holder list | held if - and incomplete | built | Held only by the sentences it happens to name. Eight more, each quoted in the findings, bear on M1, M6, M9, arms (c') and (e)/(f), P1.4, P4.5, section 1's grain, section 6's normative row, section 10's free choices and section 3's instrument argument. Semantics log S76 names five of those eight by place, so the list could have been completed from the record W4 itself cites. |
| P4, "Five, none changing a claim" | contradicts | asserted | There is a sixth, and it is the one W3's M8a rests on (Part VII's eliminative sentence). |
| P5, "sections 7 to 13 of W3" unchanged | contradicts | asserted | Those sections name file 10 as the authority four times, including the definition of what "holds" and "contradicts" mean for a judge in phase 1. |
| P6, the give-up list | held | built | It books the two real costs (an authority with no cases behind it; the unqualified consequence). It does not book two more: that phase 1's judges will carry a file-10-mapped skill, and that the quote-check program's output is now stale. |
| P7, the traps | held | built | Trap 1 is right and matters: the Semantics record does say file 11 is the candidate authority until tested, and W4 does not claim otherwise. |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** Had file 11 changed nothing that touched W3, W4 would have been a one-line note. It is fourteen paragraphs, which is the right size; the fault is not the shape but that the list stops early.

**Reverse.** Poke the cause: change file 11's Derivation 3 back and M2's restatement has to go - it moves. Poke the effect: change W4's M2 and nothing in file 11 moves. Direction is right; W4 is following the theory, not fitting the theory to the plan.

**Hunt the answer in the starting points.** W4's section 3 opens with "None of these changes what W3 predicts; each changes what holds a part." That is the conclusion of the audit stated as its premise. Had the list been drawn by working through file 11 Part by Part rather than through W3's already-flagged constructions, the eight missing items would have surfaced; every one of them sits in a Part (III, V, VI, VIII, X, XI, XIV) where W3 had flagged no construction, so nothing invited a look.

**Add a job.** I added: every W3 quotation still present in file 11 at the Part named. It ruled out a rival version of W4 in which section 4's list is complete - the Part VII sentence fails it. That is a job that killed a version, not a repeat.

**Look inside.** This test cannot bite here, and I name it as W3 section 4 and the skill require. I can compare the two documents and W4's claims about them; I cannot see how W4's list was drawn, so I cannot tell a list drawn from file 11 and truncated from one drawn from W3's flagged constructions and complete on its own terms. The part that would settle it - P3's method - is left **unknown**, with the test named: state the method in the frozen addendum.

**Pairs that pull.** P1 (follow file 11 and mark it) pulls against the fixed job of not editing HV Skill: the harder P1 is pressed, the further the judges' own skill, whose word list declares file 10 its frozen source by name and states Derivation 3 in the dropped form, drifts from the model they judge. W4 does not name this pair. It must give way on the skill's side, because W3 section 11 forbids fixing it here, so it becomes an ask - which is the forced edit in finding 4. Second pair: P5's "nothing else changes" pulls against P3's own logic, and P5 gives way.

**Check the patches.** W4 is itself a patch on a frozen plan. It records what it gives up (section 6), which is the root convention's requirement and the right form. The one narrowing made quietly is P5's blanket over sections 7 to 13.

**What the change list leaves out.** Both theory files were compared in full, Part by Part. Not compared: file 20 (set aside by S4, correctly), the R2 amendment file (never in the repository), the S76 packs.

**Build the best rival.** *The rival, put at its strongest:* keep file 10 as this plan's authority until round S76 returns, and hold W4 unfrozen. This is not mere delay. File 11 has been run against no case; the Semantics record says it "becomes the authority when the round returns and the prediction holds"; and under the rival the plan's authority and the judges' skill agree with each other, which under W4 they do not.

*What tells the two apart, in phase 1's own outputs, in the weeks before S76 returns.* Four things, each observable: (i) M2's consequence sentence and what Q2 and Q4 are said to rest on - qualified under W4, unqualified under the rival; (ii) whether each word-list row carries a "10 and 11" / "11 only" mark - under the rival every row is one file's, and there is nothing to re-derive from if S76 confirms file 11; (iii) which file `rigs/W3 quote check/` runs against - decisive, because the two files give different answers on at least one row: W3's Part VII quotation passes against 10 and fails against 11; (iv) whether phase 1 starts at all before S76 returns. Everything else - the six phases, the arms, the predictions' shapes, the skill map's rows - is the same under both, exactly as W4 section 5 says. At the level of the programme's shape the two are one explanation; the separating changes are (i) to (iv), and they are small, specific and checkable.

*Which the record's own rules favour: W4's device, on four of five rules, with one correction.*
- **Workflow decision W2**, the owner's word, recorded in this project's Decisions as written: "Here's the updated first." W3 section 7: "**The owner's word** is the sentence the owner writes, recorded in Decisions here as written". Read no wider than written, "first" tells this project to use it first. Favours W4.
- **Semantics S4**: "No no. 20 was a regression. Hence I never supplied it". S4's stated ground is regression and non-supply. File 11 was supplied, by the owner, to this project. S4 does not reach it, and W4 is right to keep file 20 set aside under it. Favours W4.
- **Root conventions**: "A new authority version is a new numbered file beside the old one"; "make the change as a new numbered file; never overwrite an old numbered file"; "Every patch records what it gives up as well as what it fixes"; "Start only after the owner's word." All four favour W4's form.
- **Planning file 2, `freezing.md`**: "an addendum records a change of transport before the first run and names what it gives up." This is the rule W4 cites and the one that does *not* cover the case; the root convention does. Finding 14.
- **The Semantics record** cuts the rival's way on one point, which W4 already concedes in trap 1 and section 6: file 11 is a candidate there, not an authority.

*What the rival buys that W4 has not booked:* under the rival, the plan's authority and HV file 33's word list agree; under W4 they do not, and nothing in W4 says so. That is the rival's one live finding, and it forces an edit (finding 4). It does not carry the rival, because under the rival phase 1 would freeze, as this project's first authority file, an M2 whose consequence W3 section 9 would itself strike - the plan already marks it as resting on attack point (D), and the Semantics record has shown that attack firing on O48. Freezing a part your own plan has marked for striking is a larger cost than re-deriving the rows marked "11 only".

*What would settle it and is not ours to run:* round S76's prediction, "O48 changes toward the thoughtful person and nothing else changes". The Semantics project runs it; this project waits and marks.

**Where the parts came from.** P1 and P2 are *built*, from the theory with the plan in view and against an outside judge's independent finding (the convergence logged at S73). P3 is *built* but drawn from W3's flagged constructions rather than from file 11, which is why it stops early. P4 and P5 are *asserted*: two claims of completeness with no stated method behind them, and both fail.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

Two things, neither large. Draw section 3 and section 4 by walking file 11 Part by Part against file 10, not by walking W3's flagged constructions - Semantics log S76 already names the places, and five of the eight missing items are on that list. And re-run the quote-check program against file 11, keeping its output beside the addendum: it is the one mechanical check that would have caught P4's miss, and the only part of this judgement a program could repeat.

## 6. What this does not show

Not that W4 is wrong to follow file 11: on the record's own rules it is right, and the owner's word says so. Not that file 11 is a better theory, a true one, or that round S76 will confirm it. Not that the fourteen findings are of one size - two must be fixed before anything runs (the sections 7-to-13 replacement; the sixth reworded quotation); the rest tighten holders that were loose before and are loose still, and a loose part is not a wrong one. Not that the list of eight missing holders is complete: I walked both files in full, but width is not something a reading like this settles, and W2's own results file says as much of the last round - "The program checks presence and the Part; it does not check width".

## 7. One next step

Before the addendum is numbered and frozen: extend W4 section 1's replacement to W3 sections 7, 9, 11 and 13; add the Part VII row to section 4; add the third item to the HV ask. Those three are forced by quotations. The eight added holders can follow in the same pass; none changes a prediction, and W4's own sentence "None of these changes what W3 predicts; each changes what holds a part" stays true of every one of them.
